note: Replace this sample bank with the official Green Horizons question file. Coordinates are WGS84. All player-facing text is English.

questions.name: Jerusalem
questions.hint: Israel's historic capital, home to the Old City and sites sacred to three faiths.

questions.name: Tel Aviv
questions.hint: A Mediterranean coastal city known for Bauhaus buildings, beaches, and nightlife.

questions.name: Eilat
questions.hint: Israel's southernmost resort city, sitting on the Red Sea next to coral reefs.

questions.name: The Dead Sea
questions.hint: The lowest place on Earth — a hypersaline lake where visitors float with ease.

questions.name: Haifa
questions.hint: A northern port city climbing the slopes of Mount Carmel, famous for terraced gardens.

questions.name: Sea of Galilee
questions.hint: Israel's largest freshwater lake, also called the Kinneret.

questions.name: Masada
questions.hint: A clifftop desert fortress overlooking the Dead Sea, reached by snake path or cable car.

questions.name: Be'er Sheva
questions.hint: Capital of the Negev and a gateway to Israel's south.

questions.name: Nazareth
questions.hint: The largest city in the Galilee, known for its ancient basilica and hillside lanes.

questions.name: Acre (Akko)
questions.hint: A walled Crusader port on the northern coast, now a UNESCO World Heritage site.

questions.name: Caesarea
questions.hint: A Roman harbor city with a seaside amphitheater built by Herod the Great.

questions.name: Jaffa
questions.hint: One of the world's oldest ports, now adjoining Tel Aviv's southern shoreline.

questions.name: Tiberias
questions.hint: A lakeside city on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee.

questions.name: Mitzpe Ramon
questions.hint: A small Negev town perched on the rim of a vast erosion crater.

questions.name: Rosh Hanikra
questions.hint: White chalk cliffs and sea grottoes on Israel's northern Mediterranean border.

questions.name: Mount Hermon
questions.hint: Israel's highest peak — and its only ski resort in winter.

questions.name: Sde Boker
questions.hint: A Negev kibbutz closely tied to David Ben-Gurion, who is buried nearby.

questions.name: Coral Beach, Eilat
questions.hint: A Red Sea reserve where snorkelers swim above a living coral reef.

questions.name: Ramat Hanadiv
questions.hint: Memorial gardens near Zichron Ya'akov, with an ancient aqueduct just below the ridge.

questions.name: Yatir Forest
questions.hint: Israel's largest planted forest, growing against the edge of the desert.

questions.name: Canada Park
questions.hint: A JNF park in the Ayalon Valley with springs, picnic groves, and ancient ruins.

questions.name: Ben Shemen Forest
questions.hint: A popular picnic woodland between Tel Aviv and Jerusalem, laced with bike trails.

questions.name: Ein Gedi
questions.hint: A desert oasis with waterfalls and ibex, tucked against the Dead Sea cliffs.

questions.name: Banias (Hermon Stream)
questions.hint: Powerful springs and a waterfall at the foot of Mount Hermon, once a Roman sanctuary.

questions.name: Tel Dan
questions.hint: A lush northern reserve with one of the oldest arched gates ever found.

questions.name: Timna Park
questions.hint: Ancient copper mines and red sandstone formations in the southern Arava.

questions.name: Hula Valley
questions.hint: Restored wetlands on a major bird-migration highway between Africa and Europe.

questions.name: Mount Tabor
questions.hint: A distinctive dome-shaped mountain rising alone from the Lower Galilee.

questions.name: Jerusalem Forest
questions.hint: A JNF green belt on the western edge of the capital, planted after 1948.

questions.name: British Park
questions.hint: A rolling JNF park in the Judean foothills, planted with the help of UK donors.

questions.name: Eshtaol Forest
questions.hint: A woodland in the Jerusalem hills, a favorite starting point for family hikes.

questions.name: Mount Meron
questions.hint: The highest peak in the Galilee, covered in Mediterranean woodland.

questions.name: Hai-Bar Carmel
questions.hint: A wildlife breeding reserve on Mount Carmel, home to animals once native to the region.

questions.name: Mount Arbel
questions.hint: Sheer cliffs and cave strongholds overlooking the western shore of the Kinneret.

questions.name: Avdat
questions.hint: A ruined Nabataean city on the ancient Incense Route through the Negev highlands.

questions.name: Beit Guvrin
questions.hint: A labyrinth of bell caves and underground complexes in the Judean lowlands.

questions.name: Martyrs' Forest
questions.hint: A JNF forest in the Jerusalem hills planted in memory of Holocaust victims.

questions.name: Aminadav Forest
questions.hint: A Jerusalem-mountains forest with sweeping views toward the coastal plain.

questions.name: Birya Forest
questions.hint: One of the Galilee's largest planted forests, looking out toward the Hula and the Kinneret.

questions.name: Lahav Forest
questions.hint: A planted woodland in the northern Negev, near an archaeological mound and Joe Alon Center.

questions.name: Ilanot Forest
questions.hint: A JNF arboretum in the Sharon where researchers test trees from around the world.

questions.name: Hulda Forest
questions.hint: A historic JNF planting site in the Judean lowlands, beside a veteran agricultural community.

questions.name: Beit Keshet Forest
questions.hint: A Galilee forest on the slopes of Mount Tabor, popular with hikers and cyclists.

questions.name: American Independence Park
questions.hint: A JNF park between Jerusalem and Beit Shemesh, dedicated by American donors.

questions.name: Neot Kedumim
questions.hint: A biblical landscape reserve that recreates the plants and agriculture of ancient Israel.

questions.name: Castel National Park
questions.hint: A hilltop fortress on the old road to Jerusalem, remembered for a key 1948 battle.

questions.name: Sataf
questions.hint: Restored hillside terraces and ancient irrigation in the Jerusalem mountains.

questions.name: Keshet Cave
questions.hint: A dramatic natural limestone arch on the Adamit ridge in the Western Galilee.

questions.name: Little Switzerland, Carmel
questions.hint: A rugged ravine of pines and cliffs in the Carmel range, named for its alpine look.

questions.name: Gamla
questions.hint: A cliffside ancient city in the Golan, known for griffin vultures and a waterfall.

questions.name: Soreq Cave
questions.hint: A hidden stalactite cave in the Judean hills, discovered while quarrying in 1968.

questions.name: Nimrod Fortress
questions.hint: A massive medieval castle commanding the road to Mount Hermon.

questions.name: Mount Gilboa
questions.hint: A ridge above the Jezreel Valley, famous in spring for wild irises.

questions.name: Yad Kennedy
questions.hint: A circular JNF memorial in the Jerusalem forest, shaped like a tree stump cut down.
